content_voiceover: This is the condensed MCMDM-1 VWD bleeding questionnaire, the tool Bowman and colleagues validated in 2008 as a shortened version of the original bleeding assessment tool. For boards, you don't need to memorize every cell, but understand the structure. Twelve bleeding symptom categories are each scored from minus one up to four, based on severity and treatment required. A score of zero is the default normal, and negative scores like minus one for surgery or tooth extraction actually reward a truly negative history, meaning multiple bleeding challenges with no bleeding at all lower the total score below zero. Scores of two typically trigger the label consultation only, three usually needs antifibrinolytics, surgical hemostasis, or curettage, and four means blood transfusion, replacement therapy, or desmopressin was required. All twelve category scores get summed into one total assigned score, which is then used to decide whether a patient's bleeding history is abnormal enough to justify VWD testing. Recognize this as the type of standardized bleeding assessment tool, or BAT, that's become standard of care before ordering VWF assays.
keypoints: Negative scores reward true negative challenges (surgery, tooth extraction)
Score 2 = consultation only; 3-4 = active intervention required
Sum of all categories = total assigned score -> triggers VWD workup
keypoint_voiceover: This condensed bleeding assessment tool sums scores across twelve categories, each rated minus one to four based on severity and treatment needed. A negative score means a true negative challenge, like surgery without bleeding. Higher scores, three and four, reflect need for antifibrinolytics, surgical hemostasis, or transfusion. The total assigned score is what determines whether the bleeding history is abnormal enough to pursue VWD testing.
